newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended up on Monday in a day ruled by futures-related trade ahead of the contract close-out deadline, dealers said.
Hectic futures activity dominated trade in the morning session of trade ahead of the close-out at noon. Industrials shot up on futures play and golds were knocked down, dealers said.
But trade quietened down in the afternoon and the market moved sideways, they said.

"It has been very quiet since 12H00 (1000 GMT). It has been pretty flat. We have seen some softening in industrials since then," James Scott, equity managing manager at Societe General Frankel Pollack told Reuters.
Volume was heavy with nearly 1.2 billion rand worth of shares traded but only about a 250 million rand's worth was traded after 1000 GMT, dealers said.
The overall index ended up 3.9 points to 7,131.0 points and the industrial index added 53.4 points to 8,380.6 points.
Gold shares were weak after futures players pushed them down. A bullion price below $352 per ounce and a stronger rand put some pressure on golds in the afternoon.
The golds index fell 20.9 points to 1,387.8.

The Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) said it recorded an all-time high for number of trades on any one day in its 109 year history. Deals amounting to 15,418 surpassed the previous record of 12,354 reached on September 16, 1996.
Dealers said there were very few major indicators due this week to help the market with direction. The market was seen moving sideways and tracking Wall Street.
Lonrho Ltd shares traded on the JSE fell after the firm, which is also listed in London, warned that its first half results could be down by about a third.
The share reached a low of 990 cents -- a 10.1 percent slide -- after the warning before ending 60 cents lower, or 5.5 percent, at 10.30 rand.
Amic's year results, with earnings per share dipping to 1,476 cents from 1,569 cents and a dividend held at 545 cents, were in line with expectations, dealers said.
Anglo shed 325 cents to 272 rand, Absa lost 55 cents to 27.15 rand, Dries down 150 cents to 44 rand and Kloof dropped 95 cents to 33.90 rand.
The June equity futures were quiet in the afternoon after brisk trade in the morning ahead of the March contracts close-out.
Dealers said the cash market was trading cheap and players said this could bring down futures. But the market was seen taking its cue from Wall Street for further direction on Tuesday.
The June all-share contract was at 6,562/75 from 6,610, the industrial contract was at 8,175/85 from 8,180 and the gold contract was at 980/90 from 1,008.
